title: Binary Search

concept.title: Halve the search range
body: In a **sorted** array you do not have to look at every element. Look at the middle one: if it is the target you are done; if the target is smaller, it can only be in the left half; if larger, only in the right half. Each step throws away half of the remaining places, so about `log2(n)` steps are enough.
Both `lo` and `hi` are inclusive limits of the part that may still contain the target. The loop ends when this part is empty.

statement: You are given a sorted array of `n` different integers (increasing order) and `q` target numbers. For each target print its index in the array (counting from 0), or -1 if it is not in the array.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` sorted integers.
The third line has the `q` targets.
outputFormat: Print `q` lines, one answer per target.

examples.note: 8 is at index 3, 1 is missing, -4 is at index 0.

hints: Look at the middle element of the part that is still possible.
If the target is bigger than the middle, continue in the right half, otherwise in the left half.
Keep `lo` and `hi` as inclusive limits and stop when `lo > hi`.

explanation: Each comparison with the middle element removes half of the remaining range, so a search takes O(log n) steps.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n) with reading, space O(1) besides the input.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
x = list(map(int, input().split()))

out = []
for target in x:
    lo, hi = 0, n - 1
    found = -1
    while lo <= hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if a[mid] == target:
            found = mid
            break
        if a[mid] < target:
            lo = mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    out.append(found)
print("\n".join(map(str, out)))
